findings.title: Do not let an unverified TOTP value bypass password verification
findings.body: Password verification above runs only when credentials.totpCode is falsy, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence and never validates totpCode. A request containing an email, a valid backupCode, and any nonempty totpCode therefore authenticates a CAL account without its password. Someone possessing a backup code can bypass the first factor simply by supplying a dummy TOTP value. Enforce password verification for backup-code authentication independently of the supplied totpCode.

findings.title: Consume backup codes atomically
findings.body: Backup codes are checked against the user snapshot fetched earlier, then the entire array is overwritten using only the user ID. Two concurrent requests can both validate and successfully consume the same supposedly single-use code. Requests consuming different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a code that was already used. Perform validation and consumption under a database lock or use a conditional update that detects a changed backupCodes value and rejects or retries the stale request.

findings.title: Support backup recovery in external-provider 2FA challenges
findings.body: The Lost access control exists only in TwoFactorFooter, while Google/SAML 2FA redirects set totpEmail and render ExternalTotpFooter, which offers only Cancel. CAL accounts converted to Google/SAML retain their enabled 2FA and generated backup codes, so these users can possess valid recovery codes but have no way to use them after losing their authenticator. A backup-only request would also be rejected by the credentials provider's non-CAL guards, which still require totpCode. Wire backup recovery into both the external challenge UI and its authentication path.

findings.title: Notify the parent when successful setup is dismissed
findings.body: After the enable endpoint succeeds, 2FA is already active, but onEnable is now called only by the backup-codes-close button. Dismissing the backup-code dialog through Escape, the backdrop, or its ordinary close control invokes onOpenChange without emitting the successful-enable callback. A caller relying on the documented onEnable callback therefore keeps stale 2FA state even though subsequent logins require it. Ensure every dismissal after successful enablement notifies the parent, or separate the success notification from closing the backup-code screen.

findings.title: Report clipboard success only after the write completes
findings.body: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise, but it is ignored and the success toast is shown immediately. If the browser rejects the write, such as when clipboard permission is blocked, the user is told that the backup codes were copied even though the clipboard is unchanged, and the rejection is unhandled. This can cause users to save unrelated clipboard contents instead of their recovery codes. Await the write and display an error rather than a success toast when it fails.

findings.title: Remove the fixed type from the new PasswordField
findings.body: The replacement PasswordField still receives type="password". PasswordField sets its visibility-dependent type before spreading the caller's props, so this explicit prop overrides type="text" whenever the visibility toggle is activated. The new Show password control changes its icon and tooltip but never reveals the password. Omit the fixed type when using PasswordField.

findings.title: Keep the password visibility control keyboard-accessible
findings.body: Adding tabIndex={-1} removes the shared Show/Hide password button from sequential keyboard navigation. There is no alternative keyboard control for this action, so keyboard-only users can no longer activate password visibility on login and other forms using PasswordField. Keep the button in the tab order or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible action.
